Notes on research software engineering: how to design, test, and document
research software, how to write it in the programming languages it is written
in, and how to use the tools it is run with. They cover research software in
the broadest sense, in academia and in industry, from the one-off script of a
PhD student to the libraries and workflows that a community or a company
relies on. Every document can be read here or downloaded as a PDF.


## [Principles](principles/index.qmd)

What holds in any programming language and with any tools: the design
principles of research software, and how to test and document it. The
principles also define the normative language, the ladder, and the terminology
that the other two parts use.


## [Languages](languages/index.qmd)

How to write research software in one programming language, such as Python,
R, SQL, or Bash: its rules and pitfalls, its common operations, and its own
tooling.


## [Tools](tools/index.qmd)

How to use the tools that research software is run, stored, tracked, and served
with, whatever its language, organized by job: containers, workflow managers,
scheduling, cloud computing, data formats, experiment tracking, and services.
